tips.title: Hold or hover for an explainer
tips.body: Most labels and numbers on this desk explain themselves. Hover over one with a mouse, or press and hold it on a phone, and a note tells you what it does.

tips.title: Injury risk starts under 30 condition
tips.body: Above 30 condition, drills are safe. Below it the risk is 10%, plus 2% for every point under 30, so 10 condition is a coin flip. A Medical Bay beside the Training Pitch cuts that by a fifth.

tips.title: Potential is speed, not a ceiling
tips.body: Potential grades show current growth speed. SUPER percentages show the chance of a 1.5x drill gain. Players with the same grade can have different SUPER chances. Neither caps attributes.

tips.title: Drill tiers survive relegation
tips.body: Buy a drill tier once and keep it for the whole career. Going down never takes it back. Upgrade the season you can afford it, not the season you feel safe.

tips.title: The Hero Cup out-earns the league
tips.body: A full cup run pays $48,000 and 212 fans, more than any league title. Wins and heroes also grow your following now, but the Cup remains the biggest crowd leap, so rest nobody in a cup week.

tips.title: Some neighbours hide a bonus
tips.body: Certain facilities unlock a bonus when the right pair shares an edge. Try different neighbours. Bert explains a pairing once you find it.

tips.title: The works crew does one job
tips.body: One build or upgrade runs at a time, so the order you queue is the order you get. Start the long cheap jobs on a week your money is already spent.

tips.title: Money buildings can be repeated
tips.body: Fan Shops pay every week and Stadium Stands improve home gates. You may build up to three of each, but every other facility is limited to one.

tips.title: A hero's wage waits for the contract
tips.body: A player who awakens keeps their old wage until the contract ends. At renewal it jumps to hero rates, three to five times what you paid. Bank for that season early.

tips.title: The licence cap grows with the club
tips.body: You can field two powered players in the lower divisions, three from D3, four in D1. Signing a fourth hero early does not put a fourth on the pitch.

tips.title: Quick Match is the same match
tips.body: Quick Match runs the same engine and lands on the same score. Turn it on in Settings when you want it. You only give up the chance to change formation, playstyle and subs while it plays.

tips.title: AUTO and MANUAL use powers differently
tips.body: AUTO fires powers when their useful moment arrives. MANUAL shows ARMED while it waits; press FIRE! only when it becomes available. Quick Match always uses AUTO.

tips.title: A better Scout Office narrows the guess
tips.body: Scout reports give a range, not a number, and the office level sets how wide: 30 either way at level 1, 18 at level 2, 8 at level 3. Upgrade before you spend big.

tips.title: Keepers are rated on reflexes
tips.body: A keeper's overall uses REF, not SHO, so big shooting numbers do not make a better keeper. Train Reflexes and little else matters.

tips.title: Unhappy players ask to leave
tips.body: Leave a player unhappy long enough and they hand in a transfer request. Once it lands you are selling from a weak position. Fix morale while it is still a number.

tips.title: There is no attribute cap
tips.body: Every stat climbs to the same ceiling of 999. An archetype adds a bonus to its favoured attributes. It never caps the rest.

tips.title: Prize money scales with the division
tips.body: Winning your division pays $20,000 in D5, plus $10,000 for each division above, up to $60,000 in D1. Runners-up take half, so promotion pays twice over.

tips.title: Tap a stat to train it
tips.body: The + button is not the only way in. Select a player, then tap the attribute you want on their file — PAC, SHO, DEF — and the drill for that stat opens straight away.
